description: The "it is easy" summary: cited facts only.

facts.text: Modern Hebrew has a simple five-vowel system, and vowel length does not change meaning.
The alphabet has 22 letters; five of them have a different form at the end of a word, so a reader meets 27 shapes.
facts.quote: The Hebrew alphabet has 22 letters. ... Five letters have different forms when used at the end of a word.
facts.note: "27 shapes" is the arithmetic 22 + 5, not a quoted figure.

facts.text: In Israel there is a more or less consistent standard of pronunciation.
facts.quote: there is a more or less consistent standard of pronunciation

facts.text: The doubling dagesh is not pronounced in Modern Hebrew, so it needs no special sound.
facts.quote: acoustically and phonologically nonexistent in Modern Hebrew

facts.text: Only bet, kaf and pe change their sound with a dagesh; gimel, dalet and tav do not alternate.
Gimel is always a hard g as in game.
facts.quote: Always a hard g as in game; never a soft g as in George.
